findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning objects are stored unencrypted by default (no enforced SSE), increasing risk of data exposure if underlying storage or backups are compromised.

findings.issue_category: no bucket ACL / public access controls defined
findings.description: No ACL is specified and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, so the bucket may fall back to permissive defaults or remain exposed to misconfiguration that allows public access.
The bucket stores ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket despite storing model artifacts, exposing data if the bucket contents are accessed inappropriately.
The bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so operational runbook data (potentially containing sensitive operational details) is stored unencrypted.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid AWS canned ACL; if Terraform accepts a custom/invalid value or this is a typo for a permissive ACL like 'log-delivery-write', it could unintentionally grant broad write/read permissions to the audit trail bucket, undermining audit integrity.

The object is uploaded to a bucket without default encryption enforced and no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id attribute is set on the object itself, so the vendor roster file (likely sensitive) is stored without encryption.

findings.issue_category: force_destroy enabled on bucket with no versioning
findings.description: force_destroy is true and there is no versioning configuration, meaning all objects can be irrecoverably deleted along with the bucket, increasing risk of data loss from accidental or malicious deletion without any recovery path.
force_destroy is true and no versioning block is configured for a bucket holding ledger export data, allowing permanent, unrecoverable deletion of sensitive financial records.
